articles.title: Why Do Leaves Change Colour?
articles.dek: Green in summer, red and yellow in autumn. What happens to the leaves?

sources.name: Forestry England: Why do leaves change colour in autumn?
Stockholm University: Why do leaves change color in autumn?

paras: It is November, and the trees in the park look beautiful. In summer, the leaves were green. Now they are yellow, orange and red. In a few weeks, many of them will be on the ground. Why does this happen? Let's find out, step by step.

First, why are leaves green? Leaves have a green colour inside them. Its name is chlorophyll. It helps the tree make food from sunlight, water and air. In spring and summer, there is a lot of sunlight, so leaves make a lot of chlorophyll. That is why they look green for many months.

In autumn, things change. The days get shorter, and there is less sunlight. At night, it gets colder too. The tree stops making chlorophyll, and the green colour slowly breaks down. In many places, this starts in September or October.

Then the hidden colours appear. Yellow and orange colours were in the leaves all the time! In summer, you can't see them, because the green is much stronger. When the green goes, the yellow and orange can finally show.

What about red leaves? Some trees make a new red colour in autumn. It often happens after bright, sunny days and very cold nights. On those sunny days, there is a lot of sugar in the leaves, and this helps make the red colour. That is why some years are more colourful than others. Maple trees are famous for their red leaves.

Finally, the leaves fall. In winter, there is not much sunlight, so the leaves can't make much food. The tree drops them to save energy and stay safe. On the ground, old leaves become food for insects and help the soil. Then, in spring, new green leaves grow again.

Try this at home on a dry Saturday in October or November. Collect some leaves of different colours. Put them inside a heavy book for a week. At the end of the week, open the book and look at all your colours!

articles.title: Where Is Biscuit?
articles.dek: Leo's hamster is not in his cage. Where can he be?
paras: Leo lives in a small flat with his mum and his little sister, Nora. They have a hamster called Biscuit. Biscuit usually sleeps in his cage next to the window. On Saturday morning, Leo opened the cage to give him some food. Then the phone rang, and Leo ran into the kitchen.
When he came back, the cage was empty. "Oh no!" Leo shouted. "Biscuit isn't in his cage!" Nora came out of her bedroom. Mum put down her coffee. Everyone started to look for the hamster.

Nora looked under the sofa. She only found an old sock and a pen. Mum looked behind the curtains and between the cushions. Leo climbed onto a chair and looked on top of the bookcase. There was no hamster anywhere.

"Let's be quiet and listen," Mum said. The flat was silent. Then they heard a small noise. Scratch, scratch. It came from the hall. Leo walked slowly along the hall and stopped in front of his school bag.

He opened the bag carefully. Inside, there were his books, his pencil case and a banana. Next to the banana was Biscuit! The little hamster was eating a piece of Leo's cheese sandwich. He looked very happy.

Leo laughed and took Biscuit out of the bag. He carried him across the living room and put him back into his cage. This time, Leo closed the door very carefully. Biscuit went to sleep in his little house.
"From now on, I'll check the cage door every time," Leo said. Nora smiled. "And maybe you should put your sandwiches in the kitchen, not in your bag!"

articles.title: Whose Is This?
articles.dek: A scarf, some trainers, a maths book: who do they belong to?
paras: Every week, things get lost at Greenhill School. Students leave them in classrooms, in the gym or in the canteen. Some students and teachers write notes and messages to find the owners. Here are some from this week.

NOTICE on the lost property box: Is this yours? Check the box outside the school office. This week we have two jackets, a blue water bottle and a black umbrella. Please ask Mrs Lopez before you take anything. After one month, we give old things to a charity shop.

Text message from Mia to Ana: Hi Ana! I think I have your scarf. It was on my chair after art class. Is it the red one with white stars? Mine is green, so it isn't mine. I'll bring it to school tomorrow!

Note on the gym door: Whose trainers are these? We found a pair of white trainers, size 38, in the changing room on Tuesday. The owner's name isn't inside. If they are yours, please come to the PE teachers' office.

Message in the class chat from Omar: Has anyone got my maths book? My name is on the front. My brother's book looks the same, but his has a blue cover and mine has a yellow one. I need it for Thursday's test!
Note on a desk: Sam, I've got your pencil case. I took it by mistake because it looks like mine. Sorry! It's in my bag now. Meet me in the canteen at lunch. Jack

Message from the head teacher: Thank you, everyone, for helping each other. Please write your name on your things. Then it is easy to see whose they are. Let's keep our school tidy and look after our things!
